receipts.detail: a row present but carrying no usable replica_count is an incomplete policy row that fails CLOSED. The schema default seeds a NEW row; it is not a reading of a row that failed to declare one, so a garbage value and an omitted column are both simply undeclared. This scenario does NOT prove the read-not-restated property - its asserts compare the constant to column.defaultValue and to 3, which a restated literal also satisfies. That property is proved by creation-default-tracks-schema-declaration (drift and re-import) and, at the production sites, by the two creation-site receipts
a partition declaring its own replica_count wins over the schema default, with the source typed, so policy is per-partition where the schema says it is

a partition with NO policy row resolves undeclared with factor 0 across six shapes including an empty ARRAY and an array carrying an own replica_count, which satisfies typeof object and would otherwise fall through to the default. Borrowing the default would invent a requirement the partition was never given and would erase the fail-closed unreadable-requirement case landed in S1. Mutation-verified: removing the guard reds this scenario

THE MEASURED DEFECT. getInitialReplicaIds handed out the declaration BY REFERENCE and replica wiring pushed into it, so inside a running cluster a minted replace-replica-<hex> made replica_operations report a desired RF of 4 where a fresh process reports 3 — the denominator of the distinct-node invariant drifted with identity churn. The getter now returns a copy, a caller mutating its copy leaves the declaration and every later reader unchanged, and the target is unmoved because it never counted identities at all. Mutation-verified: restoring the reference leak reds this scenario. The decoder INPUT surface is pinned too, and OBSERVED AT RUNTIME rather than read off the AST: a syntactic walk sees only member accesses on the decoder own parameter, so one ordinary refactor - a module helper taking the options object and reading candidateOptions.observedReplicas - passed the check while identities authorized policy inside the authority module itself. A recording proxy sees every read wherever it happens, through a helper, alias, destructure or computed access. Mutation-verified: the helper route now reds this scenario

PERSISTED policy per table, driven through the real seeding path. This receipt was vacuous: it BUILT each row from the default and asserted the decode equalled 3, so every iteration was assert.equal(3, 3) with only a string differing, and it read no per-table declaration. It now seeds the system tables for real and asserts the DISTINCT set of persisted replica_count values is exactly the one PARTITIONS declaration, that drifting that declaration moves every table together, and that a longer identity list changes no table's persisted value. It does NOT call the decoder, so it makes no claim about what any consumer resolves - a consumer computing a requirement from a table's identity-list length is the successor quest's to catch, not this one's

the target is frozen and carries exactly replicationFactor and source — no holders, replicaIds, converged or ready — so policy and runtime state stay separate surfaces. Asserted on BOTH branches, and over Reflect.ownKeys rather than Object.keys: the earlier form used a row carrying no replica_count, which returns the frozen UNDECLARED CONSTANT and never reaches the minted projection, so a key added on the declared path survived. Mutation-verified: adding holders: [] to the declared projection now reds this scenario, and previously did not red anything. The typed source STRINGS are pinned too, since comparing a target's source to the constant that produced it cannot detect a renamed value. SCOPE: the claim is about the returned projection and the exported surface. Internal memoisation inside the module - a private WeakMap cache, say - is NOT distinguished by this scenario and the receipt does not claim otherwise

an inherited Object.prototype.replica_count and an accessor-backed column each measured a target of 99 while the bar stayed green; -2, 0, 3.5, null, "3", NaN, Infinity and true were all accepted as policy. Now every one resolves undeclared, and the accessor is asserted NEVER to execute while the row is validated. Mutation-verified: weakening the own-property descriptor read, or dropping the safe-integer test, each red this scenario. Extended after review with the UNSAFE-integer case (2**53, without which Number.isSafeInteger could be weakened to Number.isInteger unnoticed), the camel-alias ACCEPTANCE case (without which the alias could be deleted unnoticed), and rows whose two spellings DISAGREE. The spelling loop used continue-on-invalid, so a rejected snake value was silently rescued by the alias: {replica_count: '9', replicaCount: 4} decoded to 4. The first spelling actually present now decides, and a disagreeing row fails closed. The accepted spelling set is MEASURED at runtime with a recording proxy row, not read out of the array literal: widening by spread from another constant left that literal byte-identical while a forged spelling decoded to factor 99, and an enumerated rejection list is only a blocklist of guessed names. The proxy records exactly which keys the decoder probes, so a spread, concat, second lookup path or pre-normalisation all red

the claim is SEMANTIC, not syntactic: if the schema-declared replica_count default changes, the creation default follows it. The probe drifts the declaration to 4 and re-evaluates, so an implementation restating a literal cannot track it and reds. How the value is obtained — lookup, helper, or a later mechanism — is not the claim, and no source-text proof is asserted

THE REAL ALIAS CHAIN. The seed phase reads INITIAL_REPLICA_IDS[table] and hands it to PartitionService as options.replicaIds; the service stored it BY REFERENCE and raft peer reconciliation pushes onto service.replicaIds, so the mutable peer list WAS the shared declaration and one minted replace-replica-<hex> raised the apparent factor for every later reader. Copying inside getInitialReplicaIds did nothing here, because this path never calls it — the first fix protected a path with no production caller. This drives the REAL PartitionService constructor with the exact production hand-off and asserts the declaration is unchanged after a replacement identity is appended. Mutation-verified: restoring the by-reference assignment reds this scenario, which nothing else caught. The seed hand-offs are now uniform: every read of a declaration goes through getInitialReplicaIds, which returns a copy. Only the two SERVICE constructor copies and the getter itself have a behavioural witness, because they are the paths that reach an in-place mutator (raft peer reconciliation pushes and splices those lists). The remaining hand-off copies are defence-in-depth with no reachable mutator today, so reverting them alone reds nothing, and this receipt does not claim they are individually proven

the SIBLING of the partition leak, left open one line short: the seed phase hands INITIAL_MESSAGE_GROUP_REPLICA_IDS to the service by reference and raft lifecycle pushes onto service.replicaIds, so one minted identity grew the declaration for every later reader. Drives the REAL MessageGroupService constructor. Mutation-verified: restoring the by-reference assignment reds this scenario

one cross-table authority leak must not be replaced by a shared default. A MESSAGE_GROUPS row was being seeded from the PARTITIONS schema default, leaving the message-group declaration read by nothing while its rows followed another table's policy. The claim is proved with TWO arrows because both schemas currently declare the SAME number: drifting the MESSAGE_GROUPS declaration moves the message-group creation default, and drifting the PARTITIONS declaration does NOT move it. A one-arrow or source-text proof cannot distinguish the two authorities while 3 == 3. Mutation-verified: re-pointing the message-group default at PARTITIONS_SCHEMA reds arrow 2 while arrow 1 stays green

the identity-count write, driven through the REAL creation path rather than asserted against source text. A self-hosted group comes up with ONE local replica; writing replicas.length persisted a DECLARED target of 1, and every later reader decodes that row as authority, so an accident of startup timing became policy. The staged row now carries the declared default, is not equal to the identity count, and decodes back through the authority to the same value. Mutation-verified: restoring replica_count: replicaIds.length reds this scenario, and NO other receipt in this set caught that mutation

THE SITE, not the constant. Review mutation A re-pointed the production message-group write at the PARTITIONS authority - the exact cross-table leak this quest claims to close - and every receipt stayed green, because nothing pinned which constant the site consumes and both schemas declare 3. An in-process re-import cannot prove it either: ESM caches by specifier, so the re-imported phase keeps the original authority module. The drift therefore happens in a FRESH process before the authority is first evaluated, and the REAL creation path is driven: the staged row follows a drifted MESSAGE_GROUPS declaration and does NOT follow a drifted PARTITIONS one. Mutation-verified: mutation A now reds this scenario

the PARTITIONS half, which had NO witness at all: review mutation B replaced the seed-registration write with a literal 1 - a bootstrap persisting a declared target of 1 for every seeded system table - and all receipts stayed green. SeedRegistrationPhase.registerSystemTables is now driven under schema drift in a fresh process, proving every seeded partitions row follows the PARTITIONS declaration and not the message-group one. Mutation-verified: mutation B now reds this scenario

receipts.detail: THE HARNESS-FIDELITY CONTROL, and the reason every receipt in this file now runs through test/bootstrap/run-anchored-scenario-helper.js. `node --test --test-name-pattern` exits 0 when the pattern matches NOTHING and prints `# tests 1 / # pass 1` for the file-level subtest, so counts cannot distinguish a match from a miss. Review mutation C renamed one scenario and the harness reported 13/13 with it never run: every receipt was a shell proving only that the FILE loaded. The runner requires the named top-level `ok <n> - <scenario>` TAP line and clears NODE_TEST_CONTEXT and NODE_OPTIONS from the child, which the self-test caught as a real defect - an inherited test context switches the reporter off TAP and would report a PRESENT scenario as absent. Mutation-verified: mutation C now reds
